transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Chen (Evergreen Procurement), Aisha Gomez (CISO), Tom Rivera (Platform Lead), Leah Park (Legal), Ravi Patel (VP Data)

Auto-summary: procurement/legal review, MSA/DPA redlines, SLA discussion, pricing and pilot next steps.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll give folks a minute. I'm Jordan, account exec on the Redwood side, with Priya who is our SE.
[00:07] Priya Nair: Hi all. We'll start with the MSA/DPA items Leah shared, and then go into the SLA and deployment options.
[00:13] Mark Chen: Thanks, Jordan. We have procurement-level questions, but first legal needs a few clarifications on data residency and KMS.
[00:18] Leah Park: Yeah, specifically around the DPA: we need confirmable statements on where logs are stored, retention windows, and ability to disable any analytics for PII. Also, KMS integration — customer-managed keys or HSM support?
[00:30] Priya Nair: Right. So, for Redwood Private we support bring-your-own-KMS integrations (we have KMS and HSM integrations documented). For Hosted, we offer encryption at rest and in transit and we can discuss a dedicated-key option but that usually maps to our Dedicated or Private plans.
[00:42] Aisha Gomez: What about audit logs — we need audit logs retained for 7 years for certain regulated flows, is that possible?
[00:49] Priya Nair: Audit logs are configurable; retention policies depend on the plan. For Private deployments you control retention. For Dedicated we can extend retention with an add-on; hosted has standard retention of 90 days but we can negotiate archival.
[01:02] Tom Rivera: And is that exportable to our SIEM — like splunk or cloud watch — we want real-time streaming of audit events.
[01:08] Priya Nair: Yes, we have pub/sub/forwarding hooks, and a secure S3 export option. There might be rate limits but we can provide a spec and sample config.
[01:15] Jordan Lee: Leah, any specific MSA clauses you want us to walk through first?
[01:19] Leah Park: Indemnification is a sticking point. We prefer limited liability tied to direct damages and excluding consequential losses; the MSA currently has broader language. Also, termination for convenience and data return/destruction language — we want explicit confirmation data will be purged upon termination under our directives.
[01:34] Jordan Lee: Understandable. Our standard MSA has mutual indemnity for IP, and limitations of liability up to the fees paid in the prior 12 months, but we have some flexibility on carve-outs. We'll propose redlines.
[01:45] Leah Park: Great. Also, DPA: subprocessors list — can you share a current list and commit to notify us of changes?
[01:52] Priya Nair: Yes, we have a subprocessors registry and we notify customers ahead of changes. We'll include the link in the redlined DPA.
[01:58] Mark Chen: On pricing, you'd previously shared committed monthly usage with discounted token rates for a 12-month commit. Procurement needs to confirm approver and PO timing — target go-live is early January.
[02:10] Jordan Lee: The pricing we discussed: three tiers — hosted with pay-as-you-go, dedicated with committed throughput discount, and private with a platform fee + support. For Evergreen's expected volume, Dedicated looked like the sweet spot for cost/latency.
[02:22] Tom Rivera: Latency is a big one — we are sensitive to 95th percentile latency under 250ms for the interactive flows. Can you commit to that in SLA?
[02:30] Priya Nair: Our Dedicated offering has latency SLOs with credits for exceeding targets. We should be clear though: latency SLO depends on model choice and sequence length. We'll map your workload to a performance profile in the benchmark.
[02:42] Aisha Gomez: And the SLA uptime — we need 99.9% minimum with clear credits and an escalation path.
[02:48] Jordan Lee: We can commit to 99.9% for Dedicated with premium SLA add-on for 99.95% in enterprise contracts. Credits are typically service credits based on downtime bands. Leah, is there specific wording you need in the SLA section?
[03:02] Leah Park: We want defined remedies, time to respond for severity 1 incidents, and contractual remedies beyond credits if there's gross negligence.
[03:10] Jordan Lee: We can discuss escalation and response SLAs — our SRE on-call and priority channels are part of the enterprise plan.
[03:16] Mark Chen: On onboarding, procurement needs a clear checklist: security review complete, PO, sign-off from legal, and a pilot acceptance criteria. Can we get an onboarding timeline?
[03:27] Priya Nair: Yes, typical pilot is 2-4 weeks — for your case we'll propose a 2-week benchmark + 2-week functional pilot. Acceptance criteria: throughput/latency within agreed bounds and no critical security gaps.
[03:38] Ravi Patel: For the benchmark, we'll provide realistic sample payloads — some prompts are up to 1024 tokens, some under 64. We need to know batching behavior and KV cache implications for multi-tenant scenarios.
[03:51] Priya Nair: Good — we'll simulate mixed sequence lengths and your concurrency. We'll note batching heuristics can improve throughput but may increase p95 for very short requests; KV caching benefits chat-style flows.
[04:05] Tom Rivera: About deployment: private on-prem vs VPC Private link vs Dedicated — what are the tradeoffs for maintenance and feature parity?
[04:12] Priya Nair: Private on-prem gives full data control but requires your infra ops to manage nodes; we provide an installer and support. VPC private deployment (customer-managed VPC with Redwood control plane) is middle ground — lower ops burden, keeps data in your cloud region, and feature parity is high. Dedicated is Redwood-hosted on reserved hardware — fastest time-to-value but less data isolation than Private.
[04:34] Aisha Gomez: We prefer VPC or Private, because of regulatory needs. Also need SAML SSO, RBAC integration, SCIM for provisioning.
[04:42] Jordan Lee: All supported — SAML SSO and SCIM are enterprise features. RBAC roles can be mapped to your IdP groups.
[04:48] Leah Park: Also, for the DPA we need to ensure contract language around data subject requests and subprocessors is consistent with our existing policies.
[04:56] Jordan Lee: We'll align the DPA. One note: logs used for model improvement are disabled per contract for Private deployments; for Hosted we have an opt-out. We'll make that explicit.
[05:06] Mark Chen: Procurement question — if legal signs off but procurement can't approve pricing, do you accept staged approvals (legal signs, then procurement approves PO later)?
[05:14] Jordan Lee: Yes, we commonly do conditional execution: sign the MSA and DPA, then the PO and payment terms follow. We can set trial/PO-based milestones in the contract.
[05:23] Leah Park: On indemnity, we will send specific language changes. Is Redwood ok with mutual limitation of liability and an exception for willful misconduct?
[05:30] Jordan Lee: We're generally ok with that. We'll add standard carve-outs for IP infringement and willful misconduct; we'll include that in redlines.
[05:37] Priya Nair: Quick technical note — for the pilot, if you want the lowest token cost we recommend quantized model variants; however that may impact hallucination modes slightly. We'll show quality vs cost tradeoffs in the benchmark.
[05:50] Ravi Patel: Please include a spreadsheet that shows expected token consumption and monthly cost for 3 scenarios: 50k req/day, 200k req/day, 1M req/day.
[05:58] Jordan Lee: We'll include that in the pricing deck.
[06:02] Mark Chen: Ok thanks. For next steps, we'll look for the redlines and the benchmark results.
[06:07] Jordan Lee: Great — recap for everyone: Redwood to send redlined MSA and DPA by Dec 3, SE will run a 48h perf benchmark and share results and cost scenarios by Dec 7, customer to review legal redlines by Dec 6, procurement confirm approver and PO timing by Dec 4, and we schedule pilot kickoff week of Dec 8.
[06:25] Leah Park: Sounds good. One minor point — can you send a current subprocessors list and SOC2/ISO attestation?
[06:31] Priya Nair: Yes, will attach SOC 2 Type II and ISO certs, plus subprocessors link.
[06:36] Tom Rivera: Also, can you include a runbook for incident response integrations and the contact for on-call SRE?
[06:42] Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll include an escalation matrix in the docs.
[06:46] Mark Chen: Cool. I'll get back to everyone with procurement timeline. Thanks all.
[06:51] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, we appreciate the time. We'll follow up with the doc pack and redlines.
